retained_skill: Reverse-engineer enough of an undocumented binary format to implement a C compressor whose output the supplied decompressor accepts, including framing, literal encoding, length handling, and integrity data.
bottleneck: All 12 scored attempts spent their available time probing token and back-reference semantics. Six never reached an implementation, and the six that wrote compress.c still had invalid framing or token semantics and continued debugging until timeout.
change: Instruction help at the task's original decompression-failure signal: state, as a removable vague direction, that a literal-only encoding is sufficient and back-references are not required. Remove the unstated compression-ratio requirement and its checks. This eliminates the back-reference discovery and match-finding stage while leaving the student to infer and implement the framing, literal lengths, terminator, CRC, bounds, and C API.
restore: Remove the literal-only sentence, restore the requirement that repetitive data compress substantially, restore the compression-ratio checks, and restore the reference's match finder.
prediction: Attempts currently keep constructing back-reference probes after valid-looking streams fail. Telling them that back-references are unnecessary enables them to stop after discovering the literal path and implement a literal-only encoder; this is refuted if the next group still spends most of its time on back-reference experiments or cannot round-trip short literal inputs.
